records.name: ALS Association equipment loan closets
records.org: ALS Association
records.description: Local ALS Association chapters keep loan closets of used and donated equipment, from bath benches to power wheelchairs, for people living with ALS. The Association is building a nationwide equipment program with a shared inventory.
records.next_step: Contact your ALS Association care team to request equipment.
constraints: For people living with ALS; a diagnosis may need to be confirmed.
Each chapter sets its own rules.

records.name: Free volunteer-built Toddler Mobility Trainer
records.org: MakeGood Inc (New Orleans)
records.description: MakeGood is a nonprofit that connects volunteer makers with children who need custom mobility and adaptive equipment. Its open-source 3D-printed Toddler Mobility Trainer, a pediatric wheelchair-style device for ages 1 to 8, can be requested free through the MakeGood Network.
records.next_step: Use the request page to ask for a volunteer-built chair for your child, and expect a waitlist.
constraints: For young children (ages 1 to 8); free requests may involve a waitlist.
Designs are open source, so you can also build or repair one yourself.

records.name: GotDME national directory of equipment lending programs
records.org: Wheel It Forward (Stamford, CT)
records.description: A national directory of organizations that lend or accept donated durable medical equipment such as wheelchairs, walkers, hospital beds, rollators, knee scooters and shower safety equipment. It was built because many local loan closets have no website of their own.
records.next_step: Search GotDME for lending programs near you, then call to confirm availability.
constraints: Listings are gathered from the programs themselves; Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: MDA Durable Medical Equipment Grant Program
records.org: Muscular Dystrophy Association
records.description: Grant program that helps reduce the cost of mobility aids, lift chairs and other durable medical equipment for people living with neuromuscular diseases. Many people learn of it through an MDA Care Center.
records.next_step: Apply through the MDA equipment assistance page or call the Resource Center.
constraints: For people with neuromuscular diseases served by MDA.

records.name: Open-source adaptive device designs
records.org: MakeGood Inc (New Orleans)
records.description: MakeGood publishes free, open-source designs for assistive devices that anyone with a consumer 3D printer can make. Files are hosted on Bambu Lab MakerWorld. A 3D-printed Toddler Mobility Trainer costs about $150 to produce.
records.next_step: Browse MakeGood designs, or contact MakeGood to ask about a custom adaptive device.
constraints: Printing and assembly are done by you or a volunteer maker; confirm fit and safety with your therapist.

records.name: Open-source mobility equipment and right-to-repair advocacy
records.org: Mobility Independence Foundation (Mount Upton, NY)
records.description: A nonprofit that designs and shares open-source mobility equipment, such as the Endurance power chair and the RozRover for children, built to be repaired, modified and improved by the people who use it. MIF also speaks up for users' right to repair. It is based in Mount Upton, New York.
records.next_step: Visit MIF to read about its designs, ask a question or donate.
constraints: MIF is a nonprofit; designs are for builders and providers, and it does not replace your insurance or clinician.
Mobility Talk's creator serves as MIF's Finance Officer.

records.name: Wheelchair Foundation: manual wheelchairs for people in need in the U.S.
records.org: Wheelchair Foundation
records.description: Provides standard manual wheelchairs to qualified people in the United States who show financial need. Applicants submit an application, a waiver and a brief medical recommendation.
records.next_step: Email info@wheelchairfoundation.org for the application packet.
constraints: Manual wheelchairs only; does not accept physical wheelchair donations.

records.name: American Stroke Association: support group finder and Stroke Family Warmline
records.org: American Stroke Association
records.description: Searchable registry of in-person and online stroke support groups, plus a Warmline that connects survivors and families with a team member for support and information.
records.next_step: Search the support group finder by zip code, or call the Stroke Family Warmline.
constraints: Registry groups are independent of the American Stroke Association.

records.name: Amputee Coalition: support groups and certified peer visitors
records.org: Amputee Coalition
records.description: Runs a national network of 300+ registered support groups, certified peer visitors who meet with people and families in person, by phone or online, and monthly virtual groups. Services are free.
records.next_step: Search the support group finder by zip code or request a peer visit.
constraints: Registered local groups are run by volunteers, not by the Coalition; confirm meeting details before attending.

records.name: Brain Injury Association of America: help finding state support groups
records.org: Brain Injury Association of America
records.description: National organization that can tell you which brain injury support groups are available in your state and offers virtual support groups.
records.next_step: Call the helpline or use the virtual groups page.
constraints: Confirm that the group is active before attending.

records.name: Muscular Dystrophy Association: community support groups
records.org: Muscular Dystrophy Association
records.description: Adult and pediatric support groups for people affected by muscular dystrophy, ALS and related neuromuscular diseases, plus young adult programs and care centers.
records.next_step: Contact the MDA Resource Center to join a group.
constraints: Groups run by chapter; check availability for your area.

records.name: National MS Society: support groups, peer connections and MS Navigators
records.org: National Multiple Sclerosis Society
records.description: Self-help support groups (in person, online and hybrid), one-on-one peer connections and MS Navigators who help find equipment and other resources. The Society does not run a national equipment loan closet.
records.next_step: Call 1-800-344-4867 to reach an MS Navigator or search for local groups.
constraints: Local loan closets exist only at some chapters.

records.name: Paralyzed Veterans of America: peer support and national service officers
records.org: Paralyzed Veterans of America
records.description: Congressionally chartered veterans organization for veterans with spinal cord injury or disease, including MS and ALS. Chapters offer peer support, adaptive sports and social events, and national service officers help with VA claims.
records.next_step: Call the PVA benefits helpline or use the find-a-service-officer page.
constraints: Membership is for veterans with spinal cord injury or disease.

records.name: Reeve Foundation Peer & Family Support Program
records.org: Christopher & Dana Reeve Foundation
records.description: Matches people affected by paralysis with certified peer mentors, and offers virtual support groups for caregivers, people with quadriplegia and people with paraplegia.
records.next_step: Call the Reeve Foundation or use the peer program page to request a mentor.
constraints: Groups are virtual; check the current schedule.

records.name: United Spinal Association peer support: mentoring and support groups
records.org: United Spinal Association
records.description: One-on-one peer mentoring plus virtual and in-person support group meetings for people with spinal cord injuries and all wheelchair users. Chapters operate nationwide, and membership is free.
records.next_step: Open the peer support page to request a mentor or find a group.
constraints: Chapter and group availability varies by area.

records.name: Rebuilding Together affiliate finder (home repair and modifications)
records.org: Rebuilding Together
records.description: National nonprofit with local affiliates that provide free home repairs and accessibility modifications, often ramps, grab bars and railings, for low-income homeowners, especially older adults, people with disabilities and veterans. Programs include Safe at Home.
records.next_step: Use the affiliate finder, call the one that covers your address and ask whether it takes accessibility projects and how long the wait is.
constraints: Services differ by affiliate. Wait times vary and many affiliates have limited funding.

records.name: VA Home Improvements and Structural Alterations (HISA)
records.org: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
records.description: Medically necessary changes to a veteran’s primary home, including permanent ramps, accessible bathrooms and widened access. Some non-service-connected needs can qualify.
records.next_step: Ask your VA care team for a clinical review and contact your VA medical facility’s Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service. Confirm your remaining lifetime benefit and obtain the HISA application checklist.
constraints: HISA excludes portable ramps, stair glides, new construction and routine home repairs. VA determines eligibility, medical necessity and the available benefit. Prepare VA Form 10-0103, a VA-written or approved prescription, owner authorization (notarized for renters), an itemized estimate and a before photograph.

records.name: VA Special Housing Adaptation (SHA) grant
records.org: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
records.description: A housing adaptation grant route with specific service-connected disability requirements.
records.next_step: Review the qualifying disability and ownership rules with VA or an accredited representative. Apply online through VA or use VA Form 26-4555; ask VA about project planning and approval before construction.
constraints: These grants require specific qualifying service-connected disabilities; a disability rating alone does not establish eligibility. Confirm the current fiscal-year maximum and any benefit already used with VA.

records.name: VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant
records.org: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
records.description: A housing grant route for veterans with qualifying service-connected disabilities.
records.next_step: Review the qualifying disability and ownership rules with VA or an accredited representative. Apply online through VA or use VA Form 26-4555; ask VA about project planning and approval before construction.
constraints: These grants require specific qualifying service-connected disabilities; a disability rating alone does not establish eligibility. Confirm the current fiscal-year maximum and any benefit already used with VA.

records.name: VA Temporary Residence Adaptation (TRA)
records.org: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
records.description: Changes to a family member’s home where a qualifying veteran or service member is living temporarily.
records.next_step: Ask VA about TRA if you qualify for SAH or SHA and are temporarily living in a family member’s home.
constraints: TRA requires SAH or SHA eligibility; it is not a general temporary-housing or renter grant.

records.name: VA adapted housing entry route: SAH and SHA
records.org: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
records.description: SAH and SHA grants help eligible veterans or service members with qualifying service-connected disabilities buy, build or adapt a home.
records.next_step: Read the eligibility list; prepare Social Security number and VA file/claim number if available.
constraints: SAH and SHA have different disability and ownership requirements. Confirm current fiscal-year limits with VA.

records.name: Alaska Developmental Disabilities Resource Connection (DDRC) and ADRC: where to start for waivers (statewide)
records.org: Alaska Department of Health, Division of Senior and Disabilities Services
records.description: The DDRC is the first stop for Alaskans with an intellectual or developmental disability and their families. DDRC staff can help you get on the waiting list (the DD Registry) for the IDD and Individualized Supports waivers. An Aging and Disability Resource Center (ADRC) can refer you to a DDRC. After you are drawn from the list, a care coordinator helps you apply.
records.next_step: Call the ADRC and DDRC toll-free line and ask to start intake.
constraints: You must qualify for Medicaid and meet an intermediate care facility level of care for the IDD and Individualized Supports waivers.
records.phone_note: ADRC and DDRC toll-free; Division of Senior and Disabilities Services in Anchorage 907-269-3666 or 800-478-9996

records.name: Assistive Technology of Alaska: loan, reuse and demonstrations
records.org: Assistive Technology of Alaska (ATLA) for Alaska DVR
records.description: Alaska's statewide assistive technology program connects people to loaned, reused and free or used equipment and holds demonstrations. It also runs the AKTradingPost web exchange. There are no age or income requirements to work with ATLA.
records.next_step: Call (907) 563-2599 or 1-800-723-2852, or email atla@atlaak.org.
constraints: Availability varies; ask what is in stock before travelling.

records.name: Centers for Independent Living in Alaska
records.org: Federally funded Centers for Independent Living
records.description: Disability-led centers that help with equipment, home access, peer support, advocacy and moving from a facility back to the community. Federally funded centers listed for Alaska: Independent Living Center (Homer, 907-235-7911); Access Alaska (Anchorage, 907-248-4777); Southeast Alaska Independent Living (SAIL) (Juneau, 800-478-7245).
records.next_step: Call the center nearest you, say what you need (ramp, equipment, peer support) and ask which counties it serves.
constraints: Service areas differ by center; confirm that yours covers your county.
Federal list covers Part C centers only; some states also have other centers.

records.name: Disability Law Center of Alaska
records.org: State Protection and Advocacy agency
records.description: The federally designated Protection and Advocacy agency for people with disabilities in Alaska. It provides information, advocacy and legal help on disability rights.
records.next_step: Call or visit the website and ask whether they can help with your situation, such as a denial, an access barrier or a rights violation, and how intake works.
records.phone_note: First number listed by the National Disability Rights Network

records.name: Alabama certified developmental disability provider directory (search by county)
records.org: Alabama Department of Mental Health
records.description: Searchable state directory of certified community providers for developmental disabilities, with the counties each serves and a phone number. Use the Statewide filter to find providers that serve all 67 counties.
records.next_step: Open the directory, choose your county and filter for Developmental Disabilities.
records.phone_note: Department of Mental Health main line

records.name: Alabama developmental disabilities regional offices (5 regions)
records.org: Alabama Department of Mental Health, Developmental Disabilities Division
records.description: Alabama Department of Mental Health runs five regional developmental disabilities offices: Region I in Decatur (401 Lee Street NE, Suite 150), Region II in Tuscaloosa (1305 James I. Harrison Jr. Parkway), Region III in Mobile (3280 Dauphin Street, Bldg B, Suite 100), Region IV in Montgomery (400 Interstate Park Drive, Suite 401) and Region V in Birmingham (631 Beacon Parkway W, Suite 211). The department also certifies over 200 community providers.
records.next_step: Call the department and ask which regional office covers your county.
records.phone_note: Department of Mental Health main line; toll-free 800-367-0955

records.name: Alabama device reuse centers (walkers, wheelchairs, DME)
records.org: Alabama Department of Rehabilitation Services, APTAT
records.description: Five community partners reuse donated walkers, wheelchairs and other durable medical equipment. Devices are available to Alabama residents regardless of income or disability status. Centers are in Montgomery, Dothan, Homewood, Huntsville and Mobile.
records.next_step: Call the center nearest you to ask what is in stock, or call 1-800-441-7607.
constraints: Stock changes; call first.
Reuse centers do not replace insurance or a clinician's fitting.

records.name: Alabama Ability Loan Program
records.org: Alabama Department of Rehabilitation Services, APTAT
records.description: A low-interest loan for assistive technology, adaptive equipment and related services, run through Alabama's Assistive Technology Act program.
records.next_step: Contact APTAT to ask about eligibility and how to apply.
constraints: It is a loan that must be repaid; terms are set by the lender.

records.name: Arkansas Developmental Disabilities Services: intake and referral (statewide)
records.org: Arkansas Department of Human Services, Division of Developmental Disabilities Services
records.description: The DDS Intake and Referral unit is the starting point for anyone who needs developmental disability services, including the CES Waiver, autism services and the waiver waitlist. You can call or submit an online request, and a specialist reaches out.
records.next_step: Call intake and referral, or submit the online referral request.
records.phone_note: DDS Intake and Referral

records.name: iCAN: equipment loans and reuse in Arkansas
records.org: Arkansas Rehabilitation Services, Increasing Capabilities Access Network
records.description: Arkansas's assistive technology program offers free equipment demonstrations, equipment loans and a reuse and recycling program for any Arkansan with a disability or health issue. It also supports a revolving loan fund for assistive technology.
records.next_step: Call 1-800-828-2799 or email info@ar-ican.org to ask about loans or reuse equipment.
constraints: Short loans have set periods; reuse stock varies.

records.name: Arkansas State AT Program: portable ramp loans
records.org: Arkansas Assistive Technology Act program
records.description: The state Assistive Technology Act program lends portable wheelchair ramps, often free, for temporary visits or to help someone leave a hospital or rehab facility.
records.next_step: Contact your state AT program and ask what ramp sizes are available.
constraints: Ramp sizes and availability vary with inventory and demand.

records.description: State division that provides supports and services for eligible Arizonans with developmental disabilities, through district and local offices. Eligibility offices are in Flagstaff (North), Chandler (East), Tucson (South) and Phoenix (Central).
records.next_step: Call the customer service center to ask how to apply and which district office serves your county.
records.phone_note: DDD Customer Service Center

records.name: ASSIST! to Independence
records.org: ASSIST! to Independence
records.description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
records.next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility. Based in Tuba City. The directory lists Apache County within the boundaries of the Navajo Nation.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
records.phone_note: Local phone listed in the ILRU national directory

records.name: INDATA — assistive technology demonstrations, loans and reuse
records.org: Easterseals Crossroads / INDATA Project
records.description: Indiana’s Assistive Technology Act project offers information, device demonstrations, lending and equipment reuse.
records.next_step: Describe the daily task or access barrier; ask about a demonstration, short-term device loan or reused equipment.
constraints: Ask about inventory, loan terms and any costs. This referral does not promise a ramp, installation or permanent equipment.

records.name: Indiana Medicaid home and community-based services screening
records.org: FSSA / DDARS / Office of Medicaid Policy and Planning
records.description: Referral to screening for Medicaid services that may support care at home, including PathWays for Aging and disability waiver programs.
records.next_step: For a new inquiry, ask your county aging agency which screening route fits. If already in PathWays, ask your health plan’s service coordinator about assessment and authorized services. For disability waivers, ask about the Health and Wellness, TBI, Family Supports or Community Integration and Habilitation route.
constraints: Different programs have different age, disability, financial and care-assessment requirements. PathWays generally serves people 60 and older, with exceptions; Health and Wellness serves people 59 and younger with a disability. Waiver waiting lists may apply; general PathWays enrollment and its HCBS waiver are distinct.

records.name: Centers for Independent Living in Indiana

records.description: Disability-led centers that help with equipment, home access, peer support, advocacy and moving from a facility back to the community. Federally funded centers listed for Indiana: The League (Fort Wayne, 260-441-0551); accessABILITY (Indianapolis, 317-926-1660); Everybody Counts (Merrillville, 219-937-5055); ATTIC, Inc. (Vincennes, 812-886-0575); Southern Indiana Center for Independent Living (Mitchell, 812-277-9626).
records.next_step: Call the center nearest you, say what you need (ramp, equipment, peer support) and ask which counties it serves.
constraints: Service areas differ by center; confirm that yours covers your county.
Federal list covers Part C centers only; some states also have other centers.

records.name: RAMP UP Indiana (IHCDA grants to ramp builders)
records.org: Indiana Housing and Community Development Authority
records.description: State program that gives grants to nonprofits to install exterior ramps for low-income homeowners at or below 80% of area median income. It funds ramp builders, not individuals.
records.next_step: Ask a local ramp nonprofit or Area Agency on Aging whether it receives RAMP UP funds; questions go to rampup@ihcda.in.gov.
constraints: Homeowners at or below 80% of area median income.
Applications are by nonprofits; check that the program is open.

records.name: Servants at Work (SAWs): free wheelchair ramps
records.org: Servants at Work, Inc.
records.description: Faith-based volunteer nonprofit that builds ADA-compliant wooden wheelchair ramps for people with permanent or long-term disabilities in low-income households. It covers 70 of Indiana's 92 counties and partners with other ramp builders elsewhere.
records.next_step: Apply through the SAWs website or call to ask about your county.
constraints: Low-income households; check your county is covered.
Waiting lists vary.

records.name: STAR Program (System of Technology to Achieve Results)

constraints: Loans are time-limited; short-term loans are 45 days or less.

records.name: Emergency and Accessibility Loan Program
records.org: Minnesota Housing Finance Agency
records.description: Helps low-income homeowners pay for accessibility needs of a household member with a disability, or for emergency repairs. The maximum loan is $27,000.

constraints: Requires meeting income limits, owning and living in the home, and keeping taxes and mortgage current.
Summary from a home-modification research center; confirm current limits.

records.name: Centers for Independent Living in Minnesota

records.next_step: Call the center nearest you, say what you need (ramp, equipment, peer support) and ask which towns or counties it serves.

Eight centers cover the state; each serves set counties.

records.description: Provides durable medical equipment and communication aids on loan to people living with ALS, using donated and new equipment, through loan closets in Albany, Buffalo, Rochester and Syracuse.
records.next_step: Contact the ALS Association chapter to register and request equipment.
constraints: For people living with ALS.

records.name: Delaware County Office for the Aging loan closet and NY Connects
records.org: Delaware County Office for the Aging
records.description: The office runs a loan closet with wheelchairs, walkers, commodes, crutches and similar equipment for elderly Delaware County clients, and hosts NY Connects for help finding services.
records.next_step: Call the office at 607-832-5750 to ask about equipment.
constraints: Loan closet service is described for elderly clients.

records.name: Durable medical equipment loan closets
records.org: Western New York Independent Living
records.description: Each of the three independent living center locations, Buffalo, Batavia and Niagara Falls, keeps a loan closet of durable medical equipment you can borrow. The agency also accepts donated items.
records.next_step: Contact the location nearest you to ask what is available to borrow.
constraints: The agency may not always be able to pick up donated items. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Equipment loan closet and assistive technology (TRAID)
records.org: Southern Tier Independence Center
records.description: Short-term loans of durable medical equipment and assistive technology, including wheelchairs, walkers, tub seats and commodes. Some items may be available at no cost when supplies allow. No prescription, referral, payment or documentation is required to borrow.
records.next_step: Call 607-724-2111 and ask for the loan closet (TRAID) coordinator to make an appointment.
constraints: Loans are short term. Appointments are required.
The main office is in Binghamton; satellite offices serve Chenango and Delaware counties.

records.name: Medical equipment loan (211 CNY listing)
records.org: Listed on 211 CNY (msrofcny.org)
records.description: Provides durable medical equipment on a short-term loan. Staff will help explore financial assistance if insurance does not cover the cost and the item is not in the loan closet.
records.next_step: Call 315-438-4790 to ask what equipment is available.
constraints: Directory listing; confirm eligibility and what is in stock.

records.name: Suffolk County TRAID loan: equipment at no cost (SILO)
records.org: Suffolk Independent Living Organization with NYS Justice Center
records.description: SILO partners with the New York State Justice Center to loan durable medical equipment and assistive devices free. A treating professional's documentation is required.
records.next_step: Contact SILO through the Suffolk County Assistive Technology Advocacy Project.
constraints: Documentation from a doctor, PT or OT is required.

records.name: TRAID: assistive technology loans and demonstrations
records.org: NYS Justice Center
records.description: Regional device loans and hands-on training for New Yorkers with disabilities.
records.next_step: Find the regional TRAID center overseeing your county; ask about suitable devices, loans and demonstrations.
constraints: Device or ramp inventory, installation and loan terms require confirmation. A trial is not a grant for permanent equipment.

records.name: Ulster County medical equipment loan closet
records.org: Ulster County Office for the Aging (RCAL)
records.description: Lends donated medical equipment to people who cannot afford to buy their own or whose insurance does not cover it. The usual loan is three months and can be extended. A fee applies for some items.
records.next_step: Call 845-331-0541 to check what is available and make an appointment.
constraints: Fee prices changed July 1, 2024; ask when you call.

constraints: Low and moderate income applicants. Renters and condo or co-op owners need extra documents. State funding is limited, so ask about waits.

records.name: Access to Home for Heroes: veteran accessibility
records.org: NYS Homes and Community Renewal
records.description: Accessibility changes and certain emergency repairs for qualifying veterans with disabilities.
records.next_step: Ask a funded local administrator about intake, veteran status, disability documentation and prior approval.
constraints: Qualifying veteran status, substantial physical limitation, income at or below 120% of area median income and primary residence rules apply. Residents apply through local administrators.

records.name: Access to Home, Doorways to Independence (New York City)
records.org: Adapt Community Network
records.description: Home modification program for people with disabilities listed by New York City as operated by Adapt Community Network.
records.next_step: Call and ask about eligibility and how to apply.
constraints: Eligibility rules apply. Confirm with the organization.

records.name: Access to Home: disability accessibility modifications
records.org: NYS Homes and Community Renewal
records.description: Accessibility modifications to a qualifying primary residence through funded local partners.
records.next_step: Find a funded Local Program Administrator; ask whether it serves your county and accepts resident applications.
constraints: Residents cannot apply directly to HCR. Documented disability, income limits and primary residence conditions apply. Local funding and owner obligations must be checked before work.

records.name: Accessibility Upgrades Program (New York City)
records.org: Rebuilding Together NYC
records.description: Home accessibility help listed by New York City for people with disabilities, including ramps, lifts, handrails and lever door handles, for homeowners or renters.
records.next_step: Call and ask about eligibility and the current wait.
constraints: Eligibility rules apply. Confirm with the organization.

records.name: Free modular ramp program (Oswego and Cayuga)
records.org: Contact Community Services
records.description: Builds and installs free modular wheelchair ramps for eligible people in Oswego and Cayuga counties, listed in a Central New York health resource directory.
records.next_step: Call the county contact and ask about eligibility and the current ramp waitlist.
constraints: Oswego line shown; the Cayuga contact is 315-255-3447. Eligibility rules apply.

records.name: Medicaid environmental modification guidelines
records.org: NY State Department of Health
records.description: State guidelines describe how home accessibility modifications, such as ramps, are authorized for Medicaid participants under Community First Choice Option services.
records.next_step: Ask your Medicaid care manager or plan how to request an environmental modification assessment and which provider to use.
constraints: Authorization rules apply and service limits are tied to medical necessity.

records.name: OPWDD assistive technology, environmental and vehicle modifications
records.org: NY Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD)
records.description: People enrolled in the OPWDD Comprehensive Waiver can request home modifications such as a ramp to the front door or a roll-in shower, plus adaptive devices and vehicle modifications. Vehicle work must be done by a NMEDA-accredited installer.
records.next_step: Ask your Care Manager to prepare the request for OPWDD review using the state guidance and review sheet.
constraints: Requires OPWDD waiver enrollment. Requests go through a care manager and an approval process.

records.name: People Inc. Environmental Modifications (EMods)
records.org: People Inc.
records.description: Helps people qualified for OPWDD services plan and complete home modifications, assistive technology and vehicle modifications, including guiding families through the OPWDD approval process.
records.next_step: Open the EMods page and use its link to ask whether you qualify.
constraints: For people qualified for OPWDD services. Service area may extend beyond Erie County; ask.

records.name: RESTORE: emergency home repairs for older homeowners
records.org: NYS Homes and Community Renewal
records.description: Local partner assistance for qualifying emergency repairs affecting home safety.
records.next_step: Ask a funded local administrator whether your repair meets the emergency criteria and whether funds are available.
constraints: Age 60+, ownership and occupancy as a primary residence, and household income at or below 100% of area median income apply. Residents cannot apply directly to HCR.

records.name: Ramp It Up wheelchair ramp program
records.org: Broome County Council of Churches (Faith in Action Volunteers)
records.description: Builds wheelchair ramps for homebound Broome County residents with volunteer youth groups and community organizations under skilled mentors. The program is income-based on a sliding scale. Applications are accepted year round, and ramps are built in summer.
records.next_step: Call 607-724-9130 ext. 323 to request an application.
constraints: Ramps are built in summer only, so there may be a wait.

records.name: Disability Rights New York intake
records.org: Disability Rights New York
records.description: Disability rights advocacy and legal assistance subject to intake and program priorities.
records.next_step: Describe the disability-related rights or access concern to the intake office.
constraints: Public visits are by appointment. Representation is not guaranteed.

records.org: Legal Aid Society of Northeastern New York
records.description: Free civil legal help for people with low income, including veterans and older adults: housing, public benefits, consumer and other civil matters. Not criminal defense.
records.next_step: Call 833-628-0087 with your county and the legal problem. New clients are interviewed by phone. Offices are in Albany, Amsterdam, Canton, Plattsburgh and Saratoga Springs; a veterans program offers civil legal advice.
constraints: Income, case type and capacity limits apply. Legal aid is not guaranteed representation.

records.name: AT Ohio Device Lending Library
records.org: Assistive Technology of Ohio, The Ohio State University
records.description: Free 30-day trials of assistive devices before purchase.
records.next_step: Browse devices, submit signed request/agreement and await approval.
constraints: Availability and loan approval vary. High-tech AAC family requests are reviewed individually; communication-app iPads, C Pens and OrCams have professional-request restrictions.
records.phone_note: Published contact; confirm current intake

records.name: Church of the Ascension Medical Loan Closet (Johnstown)
records.org: Church of the Ascension
records.description: Loans medical equipment such as wheelchairs and medical beds to anyone for free.
records.next_step: Call (614) 581-5286 or (740) 390-8048 to check availability.
constraints: Volunteer run; call first.

records.name: Device refurbishing and reutilization program
records.org: YMCA of Central Ohio / ECRN+ with Assistive Technology of Ohio
records.description: ECRN+ accepts donated adaptive equipment, assistive technology and durable medical equipment, and lends equipment in the Columbus area. Loans through the program run up to 90 days.
records.next_step: Call Assistive Technology of Ohio at 1-800-784-3425 or email atohio@osu.edu to ask about borrowing.
constraints: Service area is the Columbus and central Ohio area.
Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Goodwill Medical Equipment Loaner Program
records.org: Ohio Valley Goodwill Industries
records.description: Lets people borrow a wheelchair or knee scooter at no cost. Goodwill also accepts clean, usable wheelchairs and knee scooters as donations.
records.next_step: Contact Ohio Valley Goodwill about borrowing a wheelchair or knee scooter.
constraints: Serves Greater Cincinnati, so nearby counties may be covered. Confirm your area and current availability.

records.name: Tri-County Independent Living Center loan closet
records.org: Tri-County Independent Living Center
records.description: Lends donated mobility, medical and home modification equipment for temporary use by people with disabilities. Inventory depends on donations and returns.
records.next_step: Contact the center to ask what is in the loan closet.
constraints: The center does not buy equipment; inventory changes.

records.name: Wheels of Hope: wheelchair distribution (Canton)
records.org: Wheels of Hope
records.description: Distributes wheelchairs to people who do not have one and seeks donated wheelchairs.
records.next_step: Contact Wheels of Hope for eligibility and availability.
constraints: Listed in directories; confirm current operations.

records.name: OOD home modifications and vehicle modification
records.org: Opportunities for Ohioans with Disabilities (OOD)
records.description: Ohio vocational rehabilitation can fund home modifications and vehicle modifications when they are needed to reach an employment goal. State rules cover both services.
records.next_step: Apply to OOD vocational rehabilitation and tell your counselor which modification you need and why it supports work.
constraints: Tied to an employment goal and an OOD plan. Not a general home repair program. Approval comes before work starts.
records.phone_note: Use the OOD website to find your local office.

records.name: Ohio HOME Choice: returning to the community
records.org: Ohio Department of Medicaid
records.description: Transition coordination for eligible Ohioans moving from a long-term-care facility to a community setting.
records.next_step: Ask the facility discharge planner and HOME Choice staff to coordinate housing, supports and accessibility needs before the move.
constraints: Medicaid and other eligibility requirements apply. HOME Choice is a transition route, not an automatic ramp grant.

records.name: Ohio Home Care Waiver vehicle modification
records.org: Ohio Department of Medicaid
records.description: The Ohio Home Care Waiver can pay for vehicle modification when the state authorizes it. State rules list the driver and vehicle documents needed before approval.
records.next_step: If you are on the Ohio Home Care Waiver, ask your case manager about a vehicle modification request.
constraints: Requires enrollment in the waiver and prior authorization.

records.name: Western Reserve Area Agency on Aging — aging support
records.org: Western Reserve Area Agency on Aging
records.description: A regional starting point for meals, transportation, caregiver support and help at home. Ask which services fit the resident’s situation.
records.next_step: Call with the county, living arrangement and help needed. Ask about assessment, eligibility, costs and the next referral.
constraints: County coverage identifies the referral agency; individual programs have separate eligibility, funding and availability rules.
records.phone_note: Directory-published referral line; ask for information and assistance

records.name: Developmental disability waiver home adaptations
records.org: Ohio Department of Developmental Disabilities
records.description: Environmental accessibility adaptations may support eligible people enrolled in Ohio Individual Options or Level One waivers.
records.next_step: Ask your county board of developmental disabilities service and support administrator about assessment and authorization in the individual service plan.
constraints: DD eligibility alone does not establish waiver enrollment or funding. Adaptations must meet waiver rules; new home construction and residential-facility modifications are excluded.

records.name: Jefferson County free ramp program
records.org: United Way of Jefferson County
records.description: A volunteer program that builds handicap ramps for Jefferson County residents at no cost.
records.next_step: Call United Way of Jefferson County at 740-284-9000.
constraints: Availability depends on volunteers and materials.

records.name: Kettering Accessibility Modification Grants
records.org: City of Kettering
records.description: City grants of up to $10,000 for income-eligible Kettering homeowners who need to modify a home because of a disability, such as adding a ramp or step.
records.next_step: Contact the City of Kettering housing programs and ask for the current Accessibility Modification Grant application and income limits.
constraints: City of Kettering residents only. Grant amounts and funding change; confirm with the city.

records.name: Minor Home Repair Program (Franklin County)
records.org: Franklin County Office on Aging
records.description: County program that has installed wheelchair ramps for residents. A 2022 news report described an eight to twelve week waitlist.
records.next_step: Call the Office on Aging and ask about eligibility and the current waitlist.
constraints: Based on a 2022 news report. Confirm eligibility and current wait times.

records.name: Modcon Living Safe at Home (Franklin County)
records.org: Modcon Living (formerly Rebuilding Together Central Ohio)
records.description: Free emergency repairs and home modifications for low-income senior, disabled and veteran homeowners in Franklin County.
records.next_step: Contact Modcon Living and ask for the Safe at Home application and current waitlist.
constraints: Listed in a third-party directory that says it did not confirm the program. Check with the organization directly.

records.name: Ohio waiver home modifications
records.org: Ohio Department of Medicaid / Ohio Department of Aging
records.description: Approved home modifications can include ramps, grab bars, doorway widening and bathroom changes under qualifying home and community-based programs.
records.next_step: If enrolled, ask your waiver case manager to assess the modification and authorize it in your service plan. Otherwise ask your county aging agency or Ohio Medicaid for screening.
constraints: Medicaid coverage alone does not establish access to this service. Applicable program enrollment, assessed need, service-plan authorization, owner consent and provider requirements apply.

records.name: People Working Cooperatively home repair and modification
records.org: People Working Cooperatively (PWC)
records.description: Home repair and accessibility modifications for older, low-income homeowners and people with disabilities in the Cincinnati area.
records.next_step: Call and ask about eligibility and the current waitlist.
constraints: Listed in the national Home Modification directory. Phone may be a program line; confirm service area.

records.name: Rebuilding Together Northeast Ohio
records.org: Rebuilding Together Northeast Ohio
records.description: Free home repairs for low-income homeowners in Northeast Ohio, including Cleveland, with ramps listed among the work. Seniors, people with disabilities and veterans are priorities.
records.next_step: Call and ask whether they build ramps in your area and how long the wait is.
constraints: Listed in a third-party directory that did not confirm the program. Check with the organization.

records.name: USDA rural home repair loans and grants
records.org: USDA Rural Development
records.description: Section 504 assistance for qualifying very-low-income rural homeowners; grants help qualifying older homeowners remove health and safety hazards.
records.next_step: Use USDA’s Ohio program page to check the property and income requirements and contact a home loan specialist about an accessibility project.
constraints: Grants require age 62 or older and additional eligibility conditions. Loans and grants have different rules. This is not a statewide entitlement or a general renter program.

records.name: Disability Rights Ohio intake
records.org: Disability Rights Ohio
records.description: Ask about disability rights, discrimination, abuse or access to services.
records.next_step: Ask about disability rights, discrimination, abuse or access to services.
constraints: Published intake hours differ across DRO pages. Hours omitted pending clarification.
records.phone_note: intake, option 2

records.name: Ohio civil legal aid: find help by county
records.org: Alliance of Ohio Legal Aids
records.description: County-based referrals for civil legal problems involving housing, benefits, debt, family, safety and health.
records.next_step: Choose your county on the official directory and contact the serving legal aid program for screening.
constraints: Income, case type, conflicts and capacity affect eligibility. Representation is not guaranteed; this is not a criminal-defense referral.

records.name: Oklahoma DDS area office, Area I: Oklahoma City and Enid
records.org: Oklahoma Human Services, Developmental Disabilities Services
records.description: DDS area office. North of Interstate 40 and west of Interstate 35; offices in Oklahoma City and Enid. Oklahoma divides DDS service areas by interstate highway, not by county.
records.next_step: Call the area office for your part of the state.
constraints: Areas are set by interstate boundaries, not counties.
records.phone_note: Area office

records.name: Oklahoma DDS area office, Area II: Tulsa
records.org: Oklahoma Human Services, Developmental Disabilities Services
records.description: DDS area office. North of Interstate 40 and east of Interstate 35; office in Tulsa. Oklahoma divides DDS service areas by interstate highway, not by county.
records.next_step: Call the area office for your part of the state.
constraints: Areas are set by interstate boundaries, not counties.

records.name: Oklahoma DDS area office, Area III: Pauls Valley
records.org: Oklahoma Human Services, Developmental Disabilities Services
records.description: DDS area office. South of Interstate 40; office in Pauls Valley. Oklahoma divides DDS service areas by interstate highway, not by county.
records.next_step: Call the area office for your part of the state.
constraints: Areas are set by interstate boundaries, not counties.

records.name: Oklahoma Developmental Disabilities Services division (statewide)
records.org: Oklahoma Human Services, Developmental Disabilities Services
records.description: State division for developmental disability services. Community Waiver services come from contract provider agencies across Oklahoma, supported by a DDS case manager. Report suspected abuse or neglect at 1-800-522-3511.
records.next_step: Call the division with general questions.
records.phone_note: General line

records.name: Oklahoma Developmental Disabilities Services: apply (statewide intake)
records.org: Oklahoma Human Services, Developmental Disabilities Services
records.description: Oklahoma DDS serves people ages 3 and up with a primary diagnosis of intellectual disability, who may also have autism, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome or other developmental disabilities. The state intake specialists send you an application and take completed ones.
records.next_step: Call the DDS intake line to get an application, or ask about the waitlist.
records.phone_note: DDS intake specialists

records.name: Oklahoma ABLE Tech Device Reutilization Program
records.org: Oklahoma ABLE Tech (Oklahoma State University)
records.description: Refurbishes and reassigns gently used durable medical equipment at no cost to Oklahomans, working with the Oklahoma Health Care Authority. SoonerCare members get priority. ABLE Tech also offers short-term device loans and a 5% financial loan program.
records.next_step: Email atreuse@okstate.edu or call 405-967-6010 to ask about available equipment.
constraints: Supply depends on donations.
SoonerCare members are served first.

records.name: Centers for Independent Living in Oklahoma
records.org: Federally funded Centers for Independent Living
records.description: Disability-led centers that help with equipment, home access, peer support, advocacy and moving from a facility back to the community. Federally funded centers listed for Oklahoma: Ability Resources (Tulsa, 918-592-1235); Progressive Independence (Norman, 405-321-3203); Sandra Beasley Independent Living Center (Enid, 580-237-8508); Oklahomans for Independent Living (McAlester, 918-426-6220); Dynamic Independence (Bartlesville, 918-335-1314).
records.next_step: Call the center nearest you, say what you need (ramp, equipment, peer support) and ask which counties it serves.
constraints: Service areas differ by center; confirm that yours covers your county.
Federal list covers Part C centers only; some states also have other centers.

records.name: A New Start reuse program
records.org: Center for Independent Living of North Central PA
records.description: Accepts donated assistive technology and durable medical equipment in good condition and redistributes it through its reuse program at its Williamsport building. The center is also the local partner for TechOWL, Pennsylvania's assistive technology program.
records.next_step: Contact the center to ask what equipment is available.
constraints: Based in Williamsport. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Blessing Board: free durable medical equipment (Shaler)
records.org: Blessing Board
records.description: Nonprofit that collects durable medical equipment and gives it to people in need in Allegheny and surrounding counties.
records.next_step: Contact Blessing Board about available equipment.
constraints: Reported in news coverage; confirm current service area.

records.name: Camp Hill Borough medical equipment loan program
records.org: Camp Hill Borough
records.description: Two-month loans of wheelchairs, quad canes, walkers, portable toilets and shower seats, free of charge, for Camp Hill Borough residents.
records.next_step: Call the borough office for availability.
constraints: Camp Hill Borough residents only.
Loan period is two months.

records.name: Caring Hearts Lending Closet
records.org: Caring Hearts Lending Closet (Delaware County)
records.description: A medical lending closet that provides donated, reusable equipment to anyone in need, regardless of financial status. Hours are by appointment.
records.next_step: Call or text 484-463-7603 to make an appointment.
constraints: Appointment only. Large items such as hospital beds and chair lifts may not be accepted.

records.name: DME Reuse Program
records.org: Disability Options Network
records.description: A center for independent living that runs a durable medical equipment reuse program. It serves people with disabilities and accepts donations from anyone. Listed offices include Jeannette and Pittsburgh.
records.next_step: Call the office nearest you to ask what equipment is available.
constraints: Listed addresses: Jeannette and Pittsburgh. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Dauphin County Area Agency on Aging loan closet
records.org: Dauphin County Area Agency on Aging
records.description: Free loan closet at the county administration building in Harrisburg for senior adults living in Dauphin County.
records.next_step: Call the Area Agency on Aging to ask what is on hand.
constraints: Listed for Dauphin County seniors; confirm eligibility.

records.name: Hiland Presbyterian Church durable medical equipment lending closet
records.org: Hiland Presbyterian Church
records.description: Church-run lending closet in Pittsburgh for Allegheny County residents; it also manages a Hospital Equipment Loan Plan.
records.next_step: Visit during open hours.
constraints: Allegheny County residents; you must be able to pick up the equipment.
Open Monday-Thursday 10-2; confirm before visiting.

records.name: Jewish Family Service durable medical equipment loan closet (Lancaster)
records.org: Jewish Family Service of Lancaster
records.description: Lends wheelchairs, walkers, canes, shower stools and bedside commodes to anyone in need. Equipment is returned when no longer needed so others can use it.
records.next_step: Visit during open hours at Congregation Shaarai Shomayim.
constraints: Open Monday 10-12 and Wednesday 9-11 except Jewish holidays; confirm before visiting.

records.name: PATF: assistive technology financing
records.org: Pennsylvania Assistive Technology Foundation
records.description: Loans can finance assistive technology and home modifications, including ramps.
records.next_step: Ask about current loan terms, repayment ability, other funding and whether a limited grant can accompany an eligible loan.
constraints: This is financing, not a standalone ramp grant. Repayment is required. Any partial grant depends on loan eligibility and available funds.

records.name: PHFA ACCESS: modifications when purchasing a home
records.org: Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency
records.description: Deferred-payment modification loans for qualifying homebuyers using a PHFA homeownership loan.
records.next_step: Ask a participating PHFA lender whether the purchase and needed modifications qualify before work begins.
constraints: Tied to a qualifying PHFA home purchase; not a general grant for current homeowners. Loan becomes due on sale, transfer or non-owner occupancy.

records.name: Pennsylvania Caregiver Support Program
records.org: Pennsylvania Department of Aging
records.description: Assessment, caregiver support and potential reimbursement for eligible care costs, including certain home modifications and assistive devices.
records.next_step: Ask your local aging agency which caregiver category applies and what must be approved before an expense.
constraints: Caregiver and care receiver must be PA residents and meet a qualifying category. Reimbursement depends on income and the care plan. Enrollment in Medicaid LTSS (CHC/LIFE) is an exclusion.

records.name: Reagan's Journey pediatric equipment lending closet
records.org: Reagan's Journey
records.description: Free pediatric medical equipment and supply lending closet in Lancaster.
records.next_step: Contact the program to make an appointment.
constraints: By appointment only.

records.name: Reused and Exchanged Equipment Partnership (REEP)
records.org: Pennsylvania Initiative on Assistive Technology, Temple University
records.description: An online classifieds service that matches people who have unused assistive technology with people who can use it. It is one of the PIAT programs that can be a source of previously owned devices, usually at lower cost than new.
records.next_step: Search REEP for the device you need, or list equipment you no longer use.
constraints: Matches buyers and sellers; condition and price are set by the owner. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: TechOWL assistive technology lending library
records.org: Temple University TechOWL
records.description: Short-term assistive technology loans let Pennsylvanians try devices before purchasing.
records.next_step: Ask about equipment trials for mobility, vision, hearing or daily living and the loan process.
constraints: Device availability and loan terms must be confirmed. A trial loan does not pay for permanent home construction.

records.name: TechOWL: reused assistive equipment
records.org: Temple University TechOWL
records.description: Connects Pennsylvanians with disabilities to reused equipment through partner organizations.
records.next_step: Describe the equipment or temporary access need and ask about current inventory, local partners and fit.
constraints: Inventory and service areas vary by partner. This listing does not confirm that a ramp is currently available or that installation is included.

records.name: UPMC Medical Equipment Recycling Program
records.org: UPMC
records.description: A hospital-system program that collects, refurbishes and distributes medical equipment. UPMC reports more than 15,000 refurbished pieces distributed since the program began in 1999.
records.next_step: Ask UPMC how to request or donate equipment.
constraints: Figure is from a 2019 report. Locations include UPMC Horizon in western Pennsylvania; Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: West Shore Senior Center loan closet (Cumberland County)
records.org: Cumberland County Aging & Community Services
records.description: Free loans of wheelchairs, walkers, crutches, canes and commode chairs. Open to West Shore and Eastern Cumberland County residents, not only seniors.
records.next_step: Call for hours and availability.
constraints: Intake requires a West Shore, Eastern Cumberland or New Cumberland address.

records.name: Catholic Charities: Challenges, Options in Aging
records.org: Catholic Charities: Challenges, Options in Aging
records.description: Local aging information and referral for older adults, families and caregivers. Military service is not required.
records.next_step: Describe the help needed and ask about local assessment, meals, transportation, caregiver support or help at home. Ask which services fit the person’s age and living arrangement.
constraints: This is an aging referral contact, not a dedicated ombudsman or guaranteed funding provider. Confirm intake, eligibility, costs, waiting lists and availability.

records.name: OPTIONS: help at home for older Pennsylvanians
records.org: Pennsylvania Department of Aging
records.description: Support for residents age 60+ with unmet daily living needs; local supplemental services may include home modifications.
records.next_step: Ask your aging agency for an OPTIONS assessment and whether home modifications are available locally.
constraints: Home modifications are supplemental and depend on the local agency. PA residency, age 60+, legal residency and unmet daily functioning needs apply. Income can affect copayments.

records.name: Pennsylvania HCBS and developmental disability routes
records.org: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services
records.description: Official overview of waiver programs, including distinct physical disability and intellectual disability/autism pathways.
records.next_step: Ask DHS or your supports coordinator which program fits; request assessment before pursuing a home adaptation.
constraints: Each program has separate eligibility. Intellectual disability/autism waivers are not a generic route for every disability.

records.name: Abilities in Motion
records.org: Abilities in Motion
records.description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
records.next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility. Based in Reading.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
records.phone_note: Local phone listed in the ILRU national directory

records.name: Adaptive Modifications Program (Philadelphia)
records.org: Philadelphia Housing Development Corporation (PHDC)
records.description: Free accessibility changes such as ramps, lifts, widened doorways and accessible bathrooms for Philadelphia residents with a permanent physical disability. Homeowners, and renters with the owner's permission, may apply.
records.next_step: Contact PHDC, ask for the Adaptive Modifications Program application, and ask about the current wait time and income rules.
constraints: Home must be structurally sound and the disability permanent. Funding limits and waits apply; confirm current rules.
records.phone_note: PHDC, 1234 Market Street, 17th Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107. Use the program page for the current phone number.

records.name: Adaptive modifications (Chester County)
records.org: Housing Partnership of Chester County
records.description: Grant-funded adaptive modifications such as ramps, lifts, door and hallway widening and bathroom or kitchen changes for eligible Chester County residents with disabilities. Repayment is not required.
records.next_step: Open the PA 211 listing, read the eligibility details and use the intake link to apply.
constraints: Eligibility and funding limits apply. Confirm on the listing.

records.name: Allegheny County Whole-Home Repairs Program
records.org: ACTION-Housing
records.description: Repairs and accessibility modifications for eligible Allegheny County homeowners, including ramps, grab bars, handrails, doorway widening and bathroom changes.
records.next_step: Open the program page and use the application link.
constraints: Funding rounds open and close. Check whether applications are open.

records.name: Community HealthChoices and home adaptation screening
records.org: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services
records.description: Pennsylvania Medicaid long-term services and supports can include approved environmental adaptations for eligible waiver participants.
records.next_step: If enrolled, ask your service coordinator about assessment and home adaptation authorization. Otherwise ask the Independent Enrollment Broker about screening.
constraints: Medicaid enrollment alone does not establish modification coverage. Waiver services have functional, financial and program requirements. Ask about current approval rules and covered equipment.

records.name: Home Accessibility Program for Independence
records.org: Urban Redevelopment Authority of Pittsburgh
records.description: City of Pittsburgh program that helps residents with physical disabilities remain in their homes.
records.next_step: Read the program page and ask the URA to notify you when the next round opens.
constraints: The page says applications closed July 31, 2026. Check for the next round.

records.name: Home maintenance and modification services (Allegheny County)
records.org: Rebuilding Together Pittsburgh
records.description: Free home repairs and accessibility modifications for low-income Allegheny County homeowners. Older adults, veterans and people with permanent disabilities are priorities.
records.next_step: Call or visit the office at 7800 Susquehanna Street, Suite 102, Pittsburgh, and ask how to apply.
constraints: PA 211 lists income below 150% of the federal poverty guidelines, current real estate taxes and owner occupancy. Confirm with the organization.
records.phone_note: Use the PA 211 listing for the current phone number.

records.name: Senior Housing Assistance Repair Program (SHARP)
records.org: Philadelphia Corporation for Aging
records.description: Minor home repairs and modifications such as grab bars and railings for income-eligible Philadelphia homeowners age 60 and over.
records.next_step: Contact the Philadelphia Corporation for Aging and ask about SHARP eligibility and the waiting list.
constraints: Age 60 or over, income-eligible homeowners with a structurally sound home.

records.name: USDA Pennsylvania rural home repair
records.org: USDA Rural Development
records.description: Section 504 repair loans and hazard-removal grants for qualifying rural homeowners.
records.next_step: Check the property’s rural eligibility and ask a USDA home loan specialist about income, repair scope and current funding.
constraints: Owner occupancy, income and credit conditions apply. Grants require age 62+ and very-low income; loan rules differ.

records.name: Veterans Miracle Center Erie: ramps for veterans
records.org: Veterans Miracle Center Erie
records.description: Offers handicap ramps to disabled veterans who meet DD-214 and income requirements, free of charge, with donations welcome. Open Tuesday through Thursday, 10 am to 2 pm, or by appointment.
records.next_step: Call to ask about an application.
constraints: Veterans only; DD-214 and income requirements apply.

records.name: Disability Rights Pennsylvania
records.org: Disability Rights Pennsylvania
records.description: Intake for disability rights information, advocacy and legal assistance.
records.next_step: Describe the access or rights concern to intake and ask whether it falls within current priorities.
constraints: Intake does not guarantee representation.

records.name: Rhode Island Division of Developmental Disabilities: eligibility and application (statewide)
records.org: Rhode Island Department of Behavioral Healthcare, Developmental Disabilities and Hospitals
records.description: You apply to the Division of Developmental Disabilities for adult services. Students can apply 2 months before their 17th birthday, and a decision comes within 30 days of a complete application. You also need Medicaid eligibility to start services. The Rhode Island Parent Information Network can help you fill out the application at 401-270-0101.
records.next_step: Call the Eligibility Unit to get an application or ask questions.
constraints: Adults 18 and older with an intellectual or developmental disability diagnosed before age 22.
records.phone_note: Eligibility Unit, Cranston; Spanish line 401-462-3014

records.name: Rhode Island Assistive Technology Access Partnership (ATAP)
records.org: RI Office of Rehabilitation Services with TechACCESS of RI and OSCIL
records.description: ATAP is a statewide partnership offering device demonstrations, equipment loans and reuse of items such as hospital beds. Partners include TechACCESS of RI and the Ocean State Center for Independent Living.
records.next_step: Visit the ATAP page to find the partner for your need.
constraints: Some partner programs, such as the telephone equipment loan, have eligibility rules.

records.name: Centers for Independent Living in Rhode Island
records.org: Federally funded Centers for Independent Living
records.description: Disability-led centers that help with equipment, home access, peer support, advocacy and moving from a facility back to the community. Federally funded centers listed for Rhode Island: Ocean State Center for Independent Living (Warwick, 401-738-1013).
records.next_step: Call the center nearest you, say what you need (ramp, equipment, peer support) and ask which counties it serves.
constraints: Service areas differ by center; confirm that yours covers your county.
Federal list covers Part C centers only; some states also have other centers.

records.name: Disability Rights Rhode Island
records.org: State Protection and Advocacy agency
records.description: The federally designated Protection and Advocacy agency for people with disabilities in Rhode Island. It provides information, advocacy and legal help on disability rights.
records.next_step: Call or visit the website and ask whether they can help with your situation, such as a denial, an access barrier or a rights violation, and how intake works.
records.phone_note: First number listed by the National Disability Rights Network

records.name: Project MEND: refurbished wheelchairs and medical equipment (San Antonio)
records.org: Project MEND
records.description: A nonprofit that collects donated medical equipment, then repairs, sanitizes and refurbishes it for people in need, including wheelchairs and power chairs. It focuses on veterans with support from the Texas Veterans Commission and is a demonstration center for the Texas Technology Access Program.
records.next_step: Ask your therapist or doctor for a referral, or contact Project MEND through the Texas Technology Access Program at 1-800-828-7839.
constraints: Based in San Antonio; ask about service area and wait times.

records.name: Texas Technology Access Program
records.org: University of Texas at Austin
records.description: Assistive technology demonstrations, device trials and reuse information.
records.next_step: Describe the task or access barrier and ask about a device demonstration, short-term loan or reuse referral.
constraints: Ask about available equipment, suitability and loan conditions. Some complex devices need a professional involved. A device referral does not promise installation or permanent equipment.

records.name: Texas reuse programs listed by TTAP (Houston, El Paso, Austin)
records.org: Texas Technology Access Program
records.description: The Texas Technology Access Program lists medical equipment reuse programs in Houston (RSVP Texas, Medical Bridges), El Paso (Project C.A.R.E.) and Austin (CPath). TTAP also lends devices for 35 days with shipping included.
records.next_step: Call TTAP at (512) 232-0740 or 1-800-828-7839 for referrals and device loans.
constraints: These reuse programs are not sponsored by TTAP; confirm eligibility with each.

records.name: Independent Living Services
records.org: Texas Health and Human Services
records.description: State independent living services can include home modifications such as wheelchair ramps, stair lifts and grab bars, plus vehicle modifications.
records.next_step: Open the program page and use the contact route to ask about eligibility and applying.
constraints: Eligibility rules apply. Funding is limited.

records.name: STAR+PLUS home and community services screening
records.org: Texas Health and Human Services
records.description: STAR+PLUS HCBS offers long-term support services, with home adaptations subject to the member’s service plan.
records.next_step: Existing STAR+PLUS members: ask the health plan’s service coordinator about HCBS assessment. Other applicants: ask the ADRC about screening and the appropriate application or interest-list route.
constraints: Program-specific financial and care criteria apply. Medicaid enrollment alone does not establish HCBS or home modification coverage.
Ask the MCO service coordinator about documented need, service-plan authorization, vendor requirements and written owner permission before arranging work.

records.name: Vocational rehabilitation equipment and home modification
records.org: Texas Workforce Commission Vocational Rehabilitation
records.description: Vocational rehabilitation can buy equipment and vehicle modifications tied to a work goal. A state bid notice showed it can also seek contractors for a customer's home modification.
records.next_step: Contact your local Texas Workforce Solutions office and ask for a vocational rehabilitation counselor.
constraints: Tied to an employment goal and a VR plan. Approval comes before work starts.

records.name: Legal Aid of NorthWest Texas

records.description: Free civil legal help for people with limited income, including veterans and older adults. Not criminal defense.

constraints: Eligibility is for qualifying disabilities and there can be a waiting list.
records.phone_note: Toll-free intake line; administrative office 801-538-4200

records.name: Utah Assistive Technology Program device reuse and loan closet
records.org: Utah Assistive Technology Program
records.description: Refurbished wheelchairs, walkers, ramps, lifts and other equipment sold, loaned or rented, with locations in Logan, the Uintah Basin and Salt Lake City, plus the statewide AT4All swap site. Posted rental rates include transportable folding ramps and wheelchairs.
records.next_step: Call and ask what is in stock, current rental or purchase prices, and whether you can try the device before committing.
constraints: Prices and stock change. Confirm before you travel.

records.name: Utah Assistive Technology Program: equipment and financing
records.org: Utah State University
records.description: UATP offers device demonstrations, lending, reuse, customization and financing options.
records.next_step: Describe the task or access barrier. Ask about suitable devices, nearby locations, fees and financing.
constraints: Availability, loan terms, financing approval and fees vary. This referral does not promise permanent ramps or installation.

records.name: Utah Center for Assistive Technology vehicle modifications
records.org: Utah Center for Assistive Technology
records.description: State assistive technology center that evaluates and modifies vehicles, such as hand controls and wheelchair lifts for vans.
records.next_step: Call and ask how to get a vehicle evaluation and whether a vocational rehabilitation counselor must refer you.
constraints: Listed in a provider directory. Eligibility rules apply.

records.name: USOR Independent Living program
records.org: Utah State Office of Rehabilitation
records.description: State independent living program that works with the independent living centers. Its forms cover home installation agreements, independent living plans and vehicle modification agreements.
records.next_step: Ask your independent living center or the state office about an independent living plan and what equipment or home installation it can fund.
constraints: Program policy excludes some items, such as vehicle chassis. Funding is limited.

records.name: Utah Aging Waiver: assessment and support
records.org: Utah Medicaid
records.description: The Aging Waiver offers community support after financial and care-need screening.
records.next_step: Start with your local aging agency. Ask your case manager whether the proposed adaptation can be authorized.
constraints: Applicants must be age 65+, meet Medicaid financial eligibility and need nursing-facility level of care. Waiver capacity is limited. Medicaid enrollment alone does not establish modification coverage.

records.name: Utah Assistive Technology Foundation low-interest loans
records.org: Utah Assistive Technology Program / Utah Assistive Technology Foundation
records.description: Low-interest loans, made with Zions Bank through the Utah Assistive Technology Foundation, for devices such as wheelchairs, scooters, lifts, adapted vans and home modifications. Small grants are also described for people at or below 150% of the federal poverty line.
records.next_step: Call UATP, read the application instructions and ask what documents you need, such as an invoice with model and price.
constraints: Loan approval depends on credit, debts and income. Confirm current rates and grant rules with the program.

records.name: Utah New Choices Waiver: moving from institutional care

constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
records.phone_note: Local phone listed in the ILRU national directory
