records.name: Rampathon: free ramps for homeowners in King and Snohomish counties
records.org: Master Builders Association of King and Snohomish Counties
records.description: Annual volunteer program that builds free wheelchair access ramps for homeowners in need. Applications open each spring.
records.next_step: Watch for the application window on the MBA Rampathon page.
constraints: Annual cycle; applications have closed by May in past years.

records.name: Disability Rights Washington
records.org: State Protection and Advocacy agency
records.description: The federally designated Protection and Advocacy agency for people with disabilities in Washington. It provides information, advocacy and legal help on disability rights.
records.next_step: Call or visit the website and ask whether they can help with your situation, such as a denial, an access barrier or a rights violation, and how intake works.
records.phone_note: First number listed by the National Disability Rights Network

records.name: King County legal aid referral through 2-1-1
records.org: Northwest Justice Project and King County legal aid providers
records.description: King County residents with a civil legal problem are screened and referred to the right legal aid provider through 2-1-1. Not criminal defense.
records.next_step: Dial 2-1-1 (or 877-211-9274) weekdays 8:00 AM–6:00 PM. Interpreters are provided.
constraints: Income and case-type limits apply. A referral is not guaranteed representation.
records.phone_note: King County 2-1-1 (toll-free number)

records.name: Wisconsin Children's Long-Term Support program: apply through your county (statewide)
records.org: Wisconsin Department of Health Services
records.description: The Children's Long-Term Support program serves children with disabilities, including developmental disabilities. You start by contacting your county health and human services agency. A support and service coordinator visits your home, uses an online tool to look at your child's care needs, and helps with enrollment.
records.next_step: Call your county health and human services agency and say you want services for your child.
constraints: Children with disabilities who meet the program's eligibility rules.
records.phone_note: Use your county health and human services number

records.name: Wisconsin programs for adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities (statewide)
records.org: Wisconsin Department of Health Services
records.description: Wisconsin offers several long-term care programs for adults with intellectual or developmental disabilities, including Family Care and IRIS, the self-directed option. You enroll through your local Aging and Disability Resource Center (ADRC) or tribal aging and disability resource specialist. They complete a functional screen and help with the Medicaid application.
records.next_step: Contact your local ADRC and ask to start the long-term care functional screen.
constraints: Adults 18 and older who need long-term care and are eligible for Medicaid.
records.phone_note: Find your local ADRC through the state page

records.name: Stout Vocational Rehabilitation Institute free wheelchair clinics
records.org: UW-Stout Stout Vocational Rehabilitation Institute
records.description: University program that has offered free clinics to check, repair and clean wheelchairs.
records.next_step: Check UW-Stout SVRI for clinic dates.
constraints: Clinics held on set dates; confirm the schedule.

records.name: WisTech
records.org: Wisconsin Department of Health Services
records.description: Wisconsin's assistive technology program. Services are provided through the state's independent living centers and partners, including device demonstration, short-term device loans, and a reuse program that can provide equipment such as a wheelchair.
records.next_step: Contact your local independent living center or the WisTech program.
constraints: Loans are short term, to try equipment or as a loaner.

records.name: WisLoan
records.org: Wisconsin WisTech with independent living centers
records.description: A statewide low-interest loan program for Wisconsin residents with disabilities to buy assistive technology and equipment, make home modifications or adapt a vehicle. Applications go through your local independent living center.
records.next_step: Contact the independent living center that serves your county to apply.
constraints: Open to Wisconsin residents of all ages who have a disability.

records.name: Centers for Independent Living in Wisconsin
records.org: Federally funded Centers for Independent Living
records.description: Disability-led centers that help with equipment, home access, peer support, advocacy and moving from a facility back to the community. Federally funded centers listed for Wisconsin: Independent Living Resources (La Crosse, 608-787-1111); Options for Independent Living (Green Bay, 920-490-0500); Society's Assets (Racine, 262-637-9128); indiGO (Superior, 715-392-9118); Midstate Independent Living Choices (Stevens Point, 715-344-4210); Access to Independence (Madison, 608-242-8484); Independence First (Milwaukee, 414-291-7520); Center for Independent Living for Western Wisconsin (Menomonie, 715-233-1070).
records.next_step: Call the center nearest you, say what you need (ramp, equipment, peer support) and ask which counties it serves.
constraints: Service areas differ by center; confirm that yours covers your county.
Federal list covers Part C centers only; some states also have other centers.

records.name: Wisconsin Aging and Disability Resource Centers (find your local ADRC)
records.org: Wisconsin Department of Health Services, Bureau of Aging and Disability Resources
records.description: Wisconsin ADRCs are the local front door for adults with disabilities, including developmental disabilities, and for older adults. They give information and assistance, options counseling and help applying for long-term care programs. Wisconsin has county and multi-county ADRCs plus Tribal ADRS partner agencies. A statewide locator line connects you to the agency for your county, and FindMyADRC.org lists each one.
records.next_step: Call the statewide locator line, or search FindMyADRC.org for your county.
records.phone_note: 844-WIS-ADRC toll-free locator, with Spanish and Hmong translators

records.name: Disability Rights Wisconsin
records.org: State Protection and Advocacy agency
records.description: The federally designated Protection and Advocacy agency for people with disabilities in Wisconsin. It provides information, advocacy and legal help on disability rights.
records.next_step: Call or visit the website and ask whether they can help with your situation, such as a denial, an access barrier or a rights violation, and how intake works.
records.phone_note: First number listed by the National Disability Rights Network

records.name: West Virginia I/DD Waiver: how to apply (statewide)
records.org: West Virginia Department of Health and Human Resources, Bureau for Medical Services
records.description: The I/DD Waiver is a Medicaid program that pays for community-based supports for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. You request the application packet from the state administrative services organization, complete it and send it back by fax, email or mail. Any DHHR local office can also help.
records.next_step: Call to request the I/DD Waiver application packet.
records.phone_note: Administrative services organization; Bureau for Medical Services 304-356-4904

records.name: West Virginia Assistive Technology System
records.org: West Virginia University Center for Excellence in Disabilities
records.description: Assistive technology demonstrations, short-term device loans and reuse information for West Virginia residents.
records.next_step: Describe the task or access barrier and ask about a demonstration, trial loan or reuse option.
constraints: Ask about current devices, loan conditions and suitability. Device information does not promise an installation or permanent equipment award.

records.name: Aged and Disabled Waiver screening
records.org: West Virginia Bureau for Medical Services / Bureau of Senior Services
records.description: Medicaid home and community services for adults who meet financial and nursing-facility-level care criteria.
records.next_step: Ask how to begin an ADW application and the required medical and financial review.
constraints: Age, residency, financial and medical rules apply; enrollment and services require review and an available opening.
Home adaptations require a documented service-plan need and Operating Agency approval through the case manager; ask before arranging work.

records.name: VISIONS independent living services
records.org: West Virginia Division of Rehabilitation Services
records.description: Vision rehabilitation and independent living support for older adults with vision loss.
records.next_step: Ask VISIONS about a vision-related independent living assessment, skills training or adaptive aids.
constraints: The published VISIONS criteria include age 55 or older, not working and permanent visual impairment; the program reviews individual needs.
For other ages or employment goals, ask DRS about the appropriate vision services.

records.name: West Virginia Relay
records.org: West Virginia Commission for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing / West Virginia Relay
records.description: Telephone relay connects people who use standard phones with people who are Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind or have a speech disability.
records.next_step: Dial 711 and give the relay operator the number you want to call; ask about the relay option that fits your communication needs.
constraints: The published alternative for English voice relay is 800-982-8772. Ask about equipment or service requirements for other relay modes.

records.name: Disability Rights of West Virginia
records.org: Disability Rights of West Virginia
records.description: The state protection and advocacy organization provides disability rights information and advocacy.
records.next_step: Describe the disability-related rights concern and ask whether it falls within current services and priorities.
constraints: The organization reviews each request and cannot accept every case.

records.name: Wyoming developmental disability waivers: how to apply (statewide)
records.org: Wyoming Department of Health, Division of Healthcare Financing, Home and Community-Based Services Section
records.description: The Comprehensive and Supports waivers help people with intellectual or developmental disabilities, and some adults with acquired brain injury, get community-based services. You contact the Benefits and Eligibility Specialist for your county, choose a case manager and complete the application. Wyoming 2-1-1 can help with services while you wait.
records.next_step: Call the Home and Community-Based Services Section and ask for the Benefits and Eligibility Specialist for your county.
constraints: You must be eligible for Wyoming Medicaid and meet level of care rules.
records.phone_note: Toll-free; Cheyenne office 307-777-7531; financial eligibility unit 855-203-2936

records.name: Wyoming Assistive Technology Resources: loans and reuse
records.org: Wyoming Institute for Disabilities, University of Wyoming
records.description: WATR lends a wide variety of assistive devices to Wyoming residents and runs a reuse program where lightly used devices and durable medical equipment can be exchanged, bought or donated. Listings are on Wyoming AT4ALL.
records.next_step: Fill out the device loan request form, or call (307) 766-6187 or email watr@uwyo.edu.
constraints: Reuse items may carry a modest price; check each listing.
